summary: In Greek mythology, Phegeus was the king of Psophis in Arcadia who purified Alcmaeon after the murder of Eriphyle and gave him a daughter in marriage. When Alcmaeon later retrieved Harmonia's necklace and robe for Callirrhoe, Phegeus' sons ambushed and killed him; Alcmaeon's sons by Callirrhoe then slew Phegeus and his wife. Distinct from other figures named Phegeus.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: Phegeus was the son of the river-god Alpheus. He is said to have been the father of Alphesiboea, Temenus, and Axion, or of Arsinoe, Pronous, and Agenor. The town of Phegeia — formerly Erymanthus, later Psophis — was believed to have taken its name from him.

sections.heading: Mythology
paragraphs: When Alcmaeon, pursued by the Erinyes of his mother's murder, came to Psophis, Phegeus offered him succor and gave him his daughter Arsinoe or Alphesiboea. She received from Alcmaeon, as a wedding gift, the robe and necklace of Harmonia. Because of Alcmaeon's crime the ground became barren, and an oracle sent him to Achelous for purification; there he took Callirrhoe to wife.

Callirrhoe demanded the necklace and robe. Alcmaeon returned to Psophis claiming an oracle required him to dedicate them at Delphi; Phegeus believed him, but a servant revealed the truth. Phegeus' sons Pronous and Agenor (or Temenus and Axion) ambushed and killed Alcmaeon. According to Hyginus, Phegeus himself killed his son-in-law.

Callirrhoe prayed to Zeus that her sons by Alcmaeon grow to manhood at once; Amphoterus and Acarnan then slew Alcmaeon's murderers and afterward killed Phegeus and his wife in their palace at Psophis.
